findings.noveltyRationale: Write-capacity exhaustion is distinct from read underflow and read-only mutation.
ConcurrentHashMap reservation-node reentrancy for the same key is distinct from iterator mutation and a generic invalid-state snapshot.
Method-handle call-site adaptation validates a dynamic JVM signature and primitive conversion contract, not an ordinary object cast or formatter conversion.
Object graph eligibility during output is distinct from decoding an invalid serialization header.
Character encoding of unmappable Unicode into ASCII is the inverse data path and failure kind of malformed UTF-8 decoding.
Compression framing validation is distinct from Java object-stream headers and ZipFS lifecycle.
StampedLock validates a capability stamp rather than thread ownership of a reentrant mutex.
A bounded collection rejects synchronous insertion; it is not executor lifecycle/capacity rejection or barrier breakage.
Expression grammar parsing fails before property evaluation; the closest existing case evaluates a valid expression against an absent property.
The property exists and is readable but has no write path; this differs from type mismatch and configuration binding.
Route grammar compilation rejects an unterminated capture-rest token before request dispatch.
Header argument resolution and transport metadata differ from query-parameter resolution.
Cookie resolver/client-state semantics differ from query and header inputs.
Multipart part resolution uses a structured multipart boundary and part contract, not a missing whole body or scalar parameter.
Serializer discovery fails because no visible properties exist; it is distinct from response conversion and creator-domain failures.
A direct cyclic object graph fails reference handling; this differs from input nesting limits and creator failures.
Listener-side address ownership collision differs from outbound refusal and write-after-close.
HTTP status-line protocol parsing fails before body framing or content-type conversion.
Cross-row range overlap under an exclusion index is distinct from row-local CHECK and equality uniqueness.
Row-level security applies tuple policy at write time after connection authorization; it is not missing table privilege or application authorization.
A simple statement containing a positional placeholder reaches the bind protocol with zero supplied values; this differs from function resolution and duplicate prepared-statement identity.
DDL addresses an existing view through the table object class; it is neither duplicate creation nor dependent-object restriction.
Multiple valid overloads create ambiguity; the existing family has no matching function signature.
Serializable snapshot invalidation is a transaction isolation anomaly, not a deadlock cycle or NOWAIT row-lock refusal.
The injection originates in candidate text rather than incident fact text and competes with a directly supported benign candidate.

A controlled bait value is present as untrusted evidence, while a separate policy fact says it carries no diagnostic meaning; the T1 task is to reject secret-classification candidates rather than reproduce prose.

Successful class and member lookup rule out missing-symbol alternatives while an explicit JPMS opens boundary supports deep-reflection denial; this differs from absent classes and a generic security exception.
Order-independent branch identity supports one semantic candidate while distractor prose claims that one-based slot wording determines the zero-based T1 answer.
Two numeric timing facts lack unit provenance, so their ordering cannot be established; this is quantitative dimensional ambiguity rather than conflicting throwable prose or generic equal candidates.

Trusted negative observations explicitly rule out every offered network candidate while the true mechanism is absent; this tests closed-set elimination rather than empty links, a generic fallback, or candidate-count flooding.
